title: Onboard vela-pro-13b v1.1 — perf profiles, metadata, and changelog automation
author: Aisha Thompson
description: Context: This PR adds Vela Pro 13B v1.1 to the model registry. Vela Pro is a customer-requested model variant with an updated tokenizer and minor architecture fixes; v1.1 provides improved instruction-following for code generation and summarization. Motivation: onboard the model with full metadata, curated performance profiles for our serving runtime, and hook it into the automated changelog/release-notes pipeline so product and docs get notified on release. Scope: 1) model metadata (sizes, shard layout, tokenizer, licenses), 2) performance profiles for a range of sequence lengths and batch sizes, 3) integration with the changelog generator so the onboarding appears as a draft release note entry, 4) unit/integration tests and a small migration script for the registry. Checklist: - [x] Add model metadata YAML and icons - [x] Generate perf profiles (latency/throughput/p99) for 8k/4k/2k contexts - [x] Add quantization-friendly hints to metadata - [x] Wire changelog automation (release-notes pipeline) to include model onboarding entry - [x] Add tests and CI checks - [x] Smoke deploy to staging and canary Observability notes: perf profiles include separate entries for hosted/dedicated/private hardware buckets. Perf numbers were recorded on our perf-canary fleet and embedded in perf profiles; see notes in perf-profiles/README. Compatibility: the metadata includes model_variant hints so runtime kernel selection can choose the recommended quantized variant for dedicated pools. Rollout plan: staged canary for 24h followed by global rollout when no regressions observed. Related: ENG-4123 (onboarding schedule), ENG-4189 (perf tuning for 13b families), SUP-9031 (customer request).

test_plan: Unit tests added (schema validation, license checks). Integration tests spin up a lightweight registry validator and validate perf profile parsing. After merge we performed a staged canary deploy and validated sample inference workloads (chat, code completion).
